subject: general
question: The Megalithic site ________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Inamgaon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Inamgaon is an important archaeological site located on the banks of the river Ghod, which is a tributary of the Bhima River in Maharashtra, India.
 
• The site dates back to the Chalcolithic (Copper Age) period, approximately between 1600 BCE and 700 BCE.
 
• Excavations at Inamgaon have revealed evidence of early farming communities, including the cultivation of crops such as barley, wheat, and legumes.
 
• Artifacts found at the site include pottery, tools, and ornaments, providing insights into the daily life and culture of the people who lived there.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megalithic Culture:** Refers to a prehistoric period characterized by the construction of large stone structures or monuments, such as dolmens and menhirs.
 
• **Chalcolithic Period:** Also known as the Copper Age, this period marks the transition between the Neolithic (Stone Age) and the Bronze Age, characterized by the use of copper tools.
 
• **Excavation Techniques:** Archaeological excavations at sites like Inamgaon involve systematic digging and recording of artifacts to understand past human activities and cultures.
 
• **Ghod River:** A significant river in Maharashtra, India, it is a tributary of the Bhima River, which is part of the larger Krishna River basin.
 
• **Bhima River:** One of the major rivers in southern India, it flows through the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka and is a tributary of the Krishna River.
